items.prompt: Put the troubleshooting steps in the right order.
steps: Change one thing, then test again
Write the cause and fix in the ticket
items.explanation: Start with the symptoms and simple checks, then change things while testing. The note at the end helps similar cases get solved faster.

items.prompt: Mrs Sari's monitor at Nusa Digital suddenly went dark. What do you check first?
choices: Order a new monitor right away
The power cable, video cable, and the monitor's power button
items.explanation: Many "breakdowns" turn out to be a loose cable or a switched-off button. Check the simplest things before taking anything apart.

items.prompt: You swap the cable, change the mouse, and restart all at once, and the problem goes away. What is the downside?
choices: None, it's fixed and that's what matters
The old mouse must be broken
You don't know which change actually solved the problem
items.explanation: Change one thing at a time, then test again. That way the real cause is clear and can be written in the ticket.

items.prompt: Tap the parts of the ticket that are evidence, not rumor.

parts.text: The coworker next door says this laptop brand always breaks.
The screen shows the error message "Disk not found".
The disk indicator light does not turn on at all.
The user feels the laptop is already old.

items.explanation: Error messages and indicator lights are evidence you can trust. Opinions and rumors don't prove anything.

items.prompt: The laptop fan is covered in thick dust, so the laptop often shuts down by itself. The right decision is…
choices: Repair: clean out the dust, then test again
items.explanation: Dust can be cleaned without new parts, so Repair is enough. Replace only when there is physical damage.
